name: Alphabet

header.one_liner: Google Cloud doubled and Search still grows double digits, but Alphabet now issues shares and debt to fund the AI build.
header.thesis: Alphabet grew revenue 25% in the September quarter: Search +12%, Google Cloud +103% with a $561B cloud backlog. To pay for $132B of capex in nine months and the $29.5B Wiz deal, it stopped buybacks and raised $42.9B of new shares, $19.1B of convertible preferred and $85B of debt. Reported earnings also include $127B of investment gains, so we value it on operating earnings.

base.eps_label: FY2026E EPS excluding investment gains and losses: operating income after tax at about 17%, on 12.37B diluted shares. Reported 2026 EPS is far higher because of about $127B of mark-to-market gains.
base.rev_label: FY2026E revenue ($B): nine months $357.3B plus a fourth quarter near $140B

rev_cagr.why: Revenue grew 25% in the quarter: Search & other +12%, YouTube ads +9%, subscriptions +11% and Google Cloud +103%. Cloud's $561B backlog covers years of growth, and consensus has 2027 revenue up 27%. The base case fades total growth toward the mid-teens as Cloud's base gets larger.
rev_cagr.source: Alphabet 10-Q, quarter ended 30 September 2026 (revenue by type, revenue backlog); Yahoo consensus

margin_end.why: Operating margin was 32% in the quarter and net margin on operating earnings about 28%. Capex of $132B in nine months, twice last year's, becomes depreciation over the next several years, so the base case lets net margin slip about a point.
margin_end.source: 10-Q (income statement, cash flow); engine judgment on depreciation

share_chg.why: Alphabet bought back no stock in 2026 and issued $42.9B of new common shares; the 6.25% mandatory convertible preferred converts into about 2.5 shares each by May 2029. The base case assumes the share count rises slowly instead of falling.
share_chg.source: 10-Q (statement of cash flows; mandatory convertible preferred note)

exit_pe.why: Today's multiple is about 25x 2026 operating EPS and 19x consensus 2027. The base case settles at 21x, below the market multiple, because heavy capex and dilution lower the quality of earnings.
exit_pe.source: Engine judgment; current multiple computed from price and FY26E operating EPS

review.basis: Q3 2026 10-Q (quarter to 30 September 2026). Q4 reports in early February; this review refreshes after the print.
review.headline: Two engines now, Search and a doubling Cloud. But Alphabet has switched from buying back stock to issuing it to fund the AI build.
review.model: Alphabet earns most of its money from advertising on Google Search, YouTube and partner sites, and increasingly from Google Cloud, which rents AI computing (including its own TPU chips) and software to businesses. Subscriptions, devices and Other Bets make up the rest.

how_it_earns.v: Ads beside search results and AI answers. Half of revenue and most of the profit.
AI infrastructure, TPUs, Workspace and security (Wiz). Doubling, with $561B of backlog.
YouTube Premium and TV, Google One, Pixel.

mix.note: Reported segments. Operating margin is segment operating income over revenue; Other Bets loses money.

review.position: The largest search and video advertiser, and the third hyperscale cloud, growing fastest of the three this year.

moat.threat: AI assistants could change how people search and how ads are priced; regulators are targeting distribution deals.

$132.0B in nine months vs $63.6B; free cash flow about -$4.8B.
Nine-month other income $127.5B, mostly private-company revaluations; Q3 had an $8.2B loss.

balance.read: Still net cash, but the direction changed: Alphabet raised about $147B of debt, shares and preferred stock in 2026.

base.story: Cloud growth slows from 100% toward 40%; Search grows high single digits; dilution offsets part of EPS growth.

downside.story: AI answers cut search monetisation while capex keeps rising; more equity is issued and the multiple falls toward 16x.

upside.story: Cloud keeps doubling with rising margins and buybacks resume in 2027.

risks.how: If AI answers show fewer or cheaper ads than links, Search revenue per query falls.
Capex doubled to $132B in nine months. If AI prices fall, depreciation erodes margins.
Funding the build with shares and convertibles lowers per-share growth.
US courts and EU regulators are acting on search distribution and ad tech; remedies could raise costs or cut traffic.
$128B of private-company holdings are marked up; a reversal would hit reported earnings, though not operations.

peer_read.why_premium: Alphabet grows faster than Microsoft and Meta on consensus, with a doubling cloud and the largest search franchise.
peer_read.why_not: It trades at a discount because it now issues shares and its free cash flow turned negative, unlike Meta and Microsoft.
peer_read.peers_note: Amazon's multiple is distorted by gains on its own AI investments; compare on 2027 estimates.

questions: What does Alphabet earn on the $132B of capex?
Should a company this profitable be issuing shares?

arguments.label: Growth
arguments.text: Revenue grew 25% in the September quarter: Google Cloud +103% with $561B of backlog, Search & other +12%, YouTube ads +9%.

arguments.label: Moat
arguments.text: Search distribution, YouTube and its own AI chips and models. The threats are AI changing how search is monetised and antitrust remedies on distribution deals.

arguments.label: Profitability
arguments.text: Operating margin was 32% and Cloud earned 36%. Reported net income includes about $127B of paper gains in 2026, so we value Alphabet on operating earnings.

arguments.label: Capital
arguments.text: Capex doubled to $132B in nine months and free cash flow turned negative. Buybacks stopped and Alphabet raised $147B of shares, preferred and debt.

arguments.label: Valuation
arguments.text: {peer_line} It trades below Microsoft for faster growth, because it now issues shares.

thesis_long: Alphabet has two growth engines for the first time. Search & other grew 12% despite the arrival of AI assistants, and Google Cloud doubled to $30.7B in the quarter at a 36% operating margin, with $561B of contracted backlog. Operating income grew 30%.

The cost is a change in capital policy. Capex doubled to $132B in nine months and free cash flow turned slightly negative. Alphabet stopped buying back stock, issued $42.9B of new shares and $19.1B of convertible preferred, and borrowed $85B. Reported earnings also include about $127B of mark-to-market gains on private investments, which we exclude. On operating earnings the stock trades at about 25x this year and 19x consensus 2027.

Our base case lets Cloud growth fade, holds Search in high single digits and assumes the share count drifts up rather than down. That earns about the cost of equity over 12 months. We would turn positive if capex peaked and buybacks resumed, and negative if Search growth fell below 8%.

upside_risks.how: With operating cash flow near $170B a year, a capex plateau would restore large buybacks quickly.
If Cloud reaches Search-like margins at its current growth, earnings would grow far faster than our base case.

dcf.label: Operating EPS. Free cash flow is held down by the AI capex build, so on free cash flow the growth the price implies would be higher still

anchor.name: Google Cloud
anchor.why: Cloud valued like Microsoft: about 19.7x EV/EBIT. Conservative for a business doubling revenue with a $561B backlog.

rest.name: Google Services, after Other Bets and Alphabet-level costs

cross.why: Value Cloud like Microsoft and the price tells you what the market pays for Search, YouTube and subscriptions. EV/EBIT is approximated as next-year P/E x (1 - 17% tax).

variant_view.why: Depreciation from $132B of capex in nine months, and share issuance instead of buybacks ($42.9B of new stock in 2026 plus the mandatory convertible), hold per-share earnings below consensus, which keeps margins near today’s.
